messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: integrating Stan into Julia
parts:
On 11/29/12 5:39 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> On an unrelated note, I spoke to a friend who is part of the Julia project who was saying how great it is. I said that,
> at the very least, maybe Stan and Juila could team up to try to get some open-source $.

Doug Bates has also been pretty active around
Julia (he seems to be everywhere -- on the Eigen
list, on the Rcpp list, and on Julia's lists).

Julia uses the MIT License, which is great.

The basic language is just-in-time compiled (I
had no idea LLVM had a JIT compiler), and I don't
know how hard the integration of C++ and Julia is,
but they say they've integrated C++ libs, so it
should at least be possible.

I have no idea how hard the integration would be.
R's turned out to be a bit more challenging than we'd
hoped, and we only have one Jiqiang!

We need to find a Julia fiend who also wants MCMC
and have them integrate it. I'm happy to help out.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: integrating Stan into Julia
parts:
On Thursday, November 29, 2012 7:58:00 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
The basic language is just-in-time compiled (I
had no idea LLVM had a JIT compiler)

Indeed, LLVM has two implementations of JIT compilation! This was the underlying idea behind my post on cling

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-dev/wiUMmmDsrHw/HbZBz4sUFOsJ

Unfortunately, cling does not work with Stan yet because LLVM's original JIT compiler cannot handle inline assembly, which Eigen has a little bit of. However, LLVM's experimental but basically ready MCJIT compiler should be able to handle it but is not enabled by default yet.

Ben
